memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Join five of the curtains together, and do the same with the other five. Make loops of blue material along the edge of the end curtain in one set, and do the same with the end curtain in the other set. Make fifty loops on one curtain and fifty loops on the end curtain of the other set, with the loops opposite each other." - Exodus 26:3-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The curtains were not left as separate pieces. God gave detailed instructions for joining them — loops carefully placed along the edges, positioned so they would line up exactly opposite each other. Individually the curtains were beautiful; joined together they became a single covering for God's dwelling.

Notice how much care went into the joining. The loops had to correspond precisely, or the pieces would not fit. God cared not only about each curtain but about how they connected. The unity was not accidental; it was designed, deliberate, and required attention.

The same is true of God's people. We are not meant to remain separate pieces, however lovely we may be on our own. Scripture describes the church as a body joined and held together by every supporting ligament (Eph 4:16). Unity does not happen by accident either — it takes intention, humility, and effort to keep the connections aligned. If you have drifted from fellowship with other believers, you are a curtain lying apart from the covering. God's design has always been that we be joined together, forming something bigger than any of us could be alone.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Am I genuinely joined with other believers, or drifting on my own?
What effort might God be asking me to make toward unity with others?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You designed Your people to be joined together, not isolated. Help me pursue real connection with Your church, and give me humility to keep those bonds strong. Amen.
